text: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two major double-strand break repair pathways exploited by CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing?
choices: HDR is the default, fast, error-prone pathway active in any cell-cycle phase, while NHEJ requires a homology template and is restricted to S/G2 phase
NHEJ is the default, fast, error-prone pathway active in most cell-cycle phases, while HDR requires a homology template and predominates in S/G2 phase
Both NHEJ and HDR require an exogenous homology template and differ only in speed
NHEJ exclusively introduces precise point mutations, whereas HDR always creates frameshift indels
explanation: NHEJ is the default, error-prone repair mechanism that produces insertions/deletions (indels) and is active across most cell-cycle phases, while HDR requires a homology donor (plasmid, ssODN, or sister chromatid) and predominates in S/G2 when a repair template is available. Option A reverses the two pathways' defining properties; option C is wrong because NHEJ requires no template at all; and option D reverses which pathway produces indels (NHEJ) versus precise edits (HDR).
